# mineflayer-x

[![CI](https://github.com/colours93/mineflayer-x/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/colours93/mineflayer-x/actions)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/mineflayer-x)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mineflayer-x)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

**Minecraft Java 26.x** support for [mineflayer](https://github.com/PrismarineJS/mineflayer) and the [PrismarineJS](https://github.com/PrismarineJS) ecosystem.

First working implementation. Reverse-engineered from the 26.1 client JAR -- the first Minecraft release with unobfuscated class names.

## What works

```
SPAWN OK
Position: Vec3 { x: 5.5, y: -60, z: -2.5 }
Gamemode: creative
Time: 17760
  y-64: bedrock
  y-63: dirt
  y-62: dirt
  y-61: grass_block
  y-60: air
```

- Connect, login, spawn on 26.1 servers
- Read blocks, biomes, light from chunks
- Send chat and commands (`/say`, `/fill`, `/setblock`, `/function`)
- Position, time, game mode
- Full game data: 1168 blocks, 1506 items, 157 entities, 65 biomes

## Install

```bash
npm install mineflayer-x mineflayer
```

## Usage

Require once before creating your bot:

```js
require('mineflayer-x')
const mineflayer = require('mineflayer')

const bot = mineflayer.createBot({
  host: 'localhost',
  port: 25565,
  username: 'Bot',
  version: '26.1'
})

bot.on('spawn', () => {
  const block = bot.blockAt(bot.entity.position.offset(0, -1, 0))
  console.log('Standing on:', block?.name)
  bot.chat('/say Hello from 26.1!')
})
```

### Low-level (minecraft-protocol only)

```js
require('mineflayer-x')
const mc = require('minecraft-protocol')

const client = mc.createClient({
  host: 'localhost',
  port: 25565,
  username: 'Bot',
  auth: 'offline',
  version: '26.1'
})

client.on('playerJoin', () => {
  client.write('chat_command', {
    command: 'say Hello!',
    timestamp: BigInt(Date.now()),
    salt: BigInt(0),
    argumentSignatures: [],
    messageCount: 0,
    acknowledged: Buffer.alloc(3)
  })
})
```

## What changed in 26.1

Protocol version **775** (up from 774 in 1.21.11). Login, configuration, handshake, and status phases are identical to 1.21.11.

### Chunk format change

26.1 added a `fluidCount` field to every chunk section header:

```
Old (1.18-1.21.11):  [2 bytes] nonEmptyBlockCount | states | biomes
New (26.1):          [4 bytes] nonEmptyBlockCount | fluidCount | states | biomes
```

This 2-byte shift causes "Bits per block is too big" errors in every existing chunk parser. Discovered by decompiling `LevelChunkSection.java`:

```java
public void read(FriendlyByteBuf buffer) {
    this.nonEmptyBlockCount = buffer.readShort();
    this.fluidCount = buffer.readShort();  // NEW
    this.states.read(buffer);
    this.biomes.read(buffer);
}
```

`lib/chunk.js` provides a proper `ChunkColumn` implementation that handles the 4-byte header.

### New packets

| Direction | Packet | ID |
|---|---|---|
| Serverbound | `attack` | `0x01` |
| Serverbound | `set_game_rule` | `0x39` |
| Serverbound | `teleport_to_entity` | `0x40` |
| Clientbound | `game_rule_values` | `0x27` |
| Clientbound | `low_disk_space_warning` | `0x32` |

### Time packet

`update_time` changed from `{age, time, tickDayTime}` to `{gameTime, clockUpdates[]}` using a new `WorldClock` registry. A compatibility shim translates this for mineflayer.

## Architecture

```
lib/
  data.js       -- registers 19 JSON data files with minecraft-data
  protocol.js   -- registers 26.1 with minecraft-protocol
  mineflayer.js -- version gate + update_time shim
  chunk.js      -- ChunkColumn261 with 4-byte section header
  physics.js    -- physics feature registration

data/           -- 19 JSON files (blocks, items, entities, protocol, etc.)
                   generated from 26.1 server JAR --reports
```

## Known limitations

- `declare_recipes` and `recipe_book_add` parsed as raw buffers (complex polymorphic types, not consumed by mineflayer)
- Some `PartialReadError` warnings on non-critical packets (entity attributes format changed slightly)

## Regenerating data

Protocol data was generated by:
1. Decompiling the 26.1 client JAR with [CFR](https://www.benf.org/other/cfr/)
2. Extracting packet registration order from `GameProtocols.java`
3. Running the 26.1 server JAR with `--reports` for block/item/entity data

See `scripts/generate-protocol.py`.
